answer: A lone juniper on a knoll grows slowly, ring by ring — so gate identity maturity the same way: standing deepens only through attested work, one epoch at a time, and a cloned fleet cannot fast-forward age. Then run audits like karst groundwater: an unpredictable network of inspection paths that surface at random accounts each epoch. Attackers must keep every clone audit-ready because they cannot see where the water will rise. Age that cannot be bought, plus audits that cannot be predicted — per-identity cost that scales with fleet size and never amortizes.
